results.corrected_extracted: In the author's controlled study (Huestis, Henningfield and Cone, 1992; 6 participants, sex not stated in the review; one cigarette of 1.75% THC, about 16 mg, or 3.55%, about 34 mg; continuous blood sampling), THC was detected in plasma from the first puff; mean peaks 84.3 ng/ml (range 50-129) and 162.2 ng/ml (76-267) at 9.0 minutes; about 60% and 20% of peak 15 and 30 minutes after smoking and 5 ng/ml or less within 2 hours; detectable (limit 0.5 ng/ml) for 3-12 hours after the lower and 6-27 hours after the higher dose; large differences between people despite computer-paced puffing.
results.note: The review gives N = 6 or six subjects, never men; '6 men' is not supported at this source. All numbers are confirmed. The participants also smoked a placebo cigarette, each in a separate session.

results.corrected_extracted: 80% to 90% of THC is excreted within 5 days, more than 65% in feces and about 20% in urine; with slow return from fat, the terminal plasma half-life of THC in people with frequent use was about 4.1 days with radiolabelled THC and sensitive methods (Johansson et al., 1988), against 24 to 36 hours from shorter sampling; THC-COOH plasma half-life up to 12.6 days in one person with chronic use; terminal urinary THC-COOH half-life 3 to 4 days. The review gives fecal excretion as 30% to 65% elsewhere and the THC half-life as greater than 4.1 days in one place (card reporting issue 3).
